name: Björn Seibert
currentRole: Head of Cabinet to the President of the European Commission
mechanisms: Management of the President's Cabinet
Responsibility for strategic and interinstitutional issues
Senior-personnel and G7/G20 coordination
constraints: The College of Commissioners and EU treaties distribute authority
Council, Parliament, courts and member states constrain outcomes
Cabinet coordination is not unilateral legislative power
strongestCounterargument: The position is a powerful access and coordination node, but the EU's multi-institutional system prevents a cabinet chief from commanding the Union.

name: Ilze Juhansone
lane: Institutional coherence, policy steering and administrative continuity
mechanisms: Steers and coordinates Commission work
Ensures alignment with presidential political guidelines
Maintains administrative coherence across policy cycles
constraints: Acts under the President and College
EU law and political institutions set legal boundaries
Administrative steering is not ownership or private command
strongestCounterargument: The Secretariat-General is central to process, but it serves a legally plural institution and cannot replace political or legislative decision-makers.

name: Sergei Kiriyenko
currentRole: First Deputy Chief of Staff of the Presidential Executive Office of Russia
mechanisms: First deputy chief-of-staff role
Executive-office coordination
Implementation and political-management pathways
constraints: Delegated office rather than independent sovereignty
Formal government and security bodies retain separate powers
Public sources do not establish every internal portfolio
strongestCounterargument: The title establishes senior proximity and administrative reach, but not personal control over all Russian politics or institutions.

name: Wang Huning
currentRole: Chairman of the CPPCC National Committee and member of the CPC Politburo Standing Committee
lane: Political consultation, consensus-building and ideological-policy integration
mechanisms: Politburo Standing Committee membership
Leadership of the top political advisory body
Consensus and consultative agenda coordination
constraints: CPPCC is consultative rather than a unilateral executive authority
Party institutions collectively determine major policy
Public records do not prove authorship of every ideology or decision
strongestCounterargument: The role can shape consensus and political framing, but it is not an independent command office.

name: Khaldoon Khalifa Al Mubarak
currentRole: Managing Director and Group CEO of Mubadala; Chairman of the Executive Affairs Authority
lane: Sovereign-investment execution, strategic policy advice and international partnerships
accessTo: Mubadala Board and Government of Abu Dhabi
President of the UAE through the Executive Affairs Authority
mechanisms: Delegated executive authority at Mubadala
Leadership of the Executive Affairs Authority
Investment Committee participation and international envoy roles
documentedReach: Strategic policy advice and bilateral relationships
constraints: Mubadala board and shareholder mandate
Government decisions remain with formal state authorities
Foreign companies and partners retain independent governance
strongestCounterargument: The portfolio of roles creates broad access, but is still bounded by boards, state authority and contractual governance.

name: Sergei Shoigu
currentRole: Secretary of the Security Council of the Russian Federation
lane: Security-policy coordination and classified interagency access
mechanisms: Security Council secretariat leadership
Interagency security-policy coordination
Access to classified assessments and senior security officials
constraints: The President chairs the Security Council
Military and intelligence agencies have separate chains of command
Public records cannot show all classified processes
strongestCounterargument: Security Council access is significant, but the secretary coordinates rather than personally commanding every force or agency.

name: Rob Goldstein
lane: Operating control, Aladdin and institutional connectivity
accessTo: Larry Fink and BlackRock executive leadership
Investment, client, risk and technology functions
mechanisms: Day-to-day global operating oversight
Connectivity across investment, client, risk and technology functions
Oversight of Aladdin and operating platforms
constraints: BlackRock acts under client mandates, fiduciary duties and regulation
Aladdin users retain their own decisions and governance
Operational reach is not ownership of client assets
strongestCounterargument: Platform centrality can create visibility and dependency, but does not turn the COO into the controller of clients or markets.

name: Philipp Hildebrand
lane: Government, central-bank and major-client relationship bridge
mechanisms: Responsibility for major client and government relationships
Prior SNB, BIS, IMF and FSB leadership experience
Membership in international policy and institutional networks
constraints: No current statutory authority over prior institutions
Professional relationships do not prove improper influence
BlackRock's decisions remain governed by corporate and fiduciary duties
strongestCounterargument: A revolving-door network creates access and expertise, but not secret command or continuing public authority.
